lines: This video has no camera, no editor and no voice actor. It's a React component and a script of eight lines.
Each line of the script becomes one scene. The narration decides how long every scene runs, so nobody drags clips along a timeline.
The voice comes back with a time for every word. Anything on screen can wait for its word, like this message, which lands right now.
Captions are cut into short pieces at the punctuation. The same pieces become an SRT file, so YouTube's captions match the picture.
No voice key yet? Captions-only mode spreads the words at a steady pace, so you can lay out and review every scene before you spend a credit.
Render it tall for Shorts, Reels and TikTok. Or render the wide cut: the same video in the middle, a headline on the left, and the running state on the right.
Then one command levels the audio to minus fourteen LUFS, and a review sheet shows a still from every scene on one page.
Write the script, render the video, and change a line whenever the facts change.
